## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Because corresponding sections occur in other early Buddhist vinayas, its core predates the initial sectarian schisms [Norman 1983]. While preserved as an independent chapter on nuns in the Pāli, Dharmaguptaka, and Mahīśāsaka traditions, the Mūlasarvāstivāda and Sarvāstivāda Vinayas do not preserve it as an independent vastu, instead incorporating these ordination accounts and rules into the *Kṣudrakavastu* [Clarke 2014; Clarke, Vinayas; Tsedroen, Brief history of the Vinaya].
